clue.text: Cloth intended for the home? Just the reverse!

definitions.text: Cloth intended for the home? Just the reverse!

parts.words: Cloth intended for the home? Just the reverse!
parts.note: 'the cloth' is the clergy, so turn the phrase round: not a clergyman meant for a house but a house meant for the clergyman

explanation.walkthrough: 'The cloth' is a set term for the clergy, so 'cloth' stands for a clergyman. Swapping the two halves as instructed gives a home intended for the parish priest.
explanation.definitionFit: The parish priest's official residence is the house set aside for that clergyman.

clue.text: The prevailing type of man?

parts.note: 'prevailing' means winning, so the man who prevails is the one who wins a contest

explanation.definitionFit: Someone who prevails in a contest is its winner, the conqueror.

clue.text: Egyptian king reads Poe's novel after church

indicators.note: 'after church' places the shuffled letters behind the church abbreviation
novel as an adjective means new, so the letters of Poe's take a new order

explanation.surface: A pharaoh sits reading an Edgar Allan Poe story after the church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a book Poe wrote, but it is the anagram signal: POES rearranged gives EOPS, placed after CH.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheops was the Fourth Dynasty pharaoh who built the Great Pyramid at Giza.

clue.text: Keeping about ten, one is in the fashion.

parts.note: RE means about or concerning, as in business letters
taken as written

indicators.note: 'one is in' puts the single letter for one inside the word for fashion

parts.note: 'the ton' is an old word for high fashion or fashionable society
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone holds on to roughly ten items, one of them being the latest style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ton' as fashion (from French) is a crossword convention worth knowing: TON with I inside gives TION, after RE and TEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Retention is the act of holding on to something, a synonym of keeping as a noun.

clue.text: Campers' requirements reasons these must be replaced

parts.note: grounds are reasons, as in 'grounds for complaint'

indicators.note: the letters of these must be put back in a different order, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A list of what campers need, with an instruction that these items should be swapped out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must be replaced' rearranges THESE into HEETS, which follows GROUNDS.
explanation.definitionFit: Waterproof sheets laid under a tent's floor are standard camping kit.

clue.text: Unit of foot, like the infantry marching

explanation.definitionFit: The arched middle of the foot is one part of it; soldiers marching in time are moving in step.

clue.text: Welsh town without water — Holyhead ?

parts.note: a drink taken neat has no water or mixer added
read as 'Holy head', the head of Holy is its first letter, H

explanation.surface: A Welsh port with no water supply: is that Holyhead?
explanation.walkthrough: Holyhead is a real Welsh port, a decoy town; split it as 'Holy' plus 'head' to get the first letter of Holy, after NEAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Neath is a town in south Wales, near Swansea.

clue.text: Experimental vessel ends up in Tees, unfinished

indicators.note: 'in Tees' sets the turned word inside the shortened river name
a word left unfinished loses its last letter, so the river name drops its final S
in a down clue 'up' means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: butts are ends, as in cigarette ends

explanation.surface: Something experimental ends up in the river Tees before it is complete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ends up' reads as 'finishes in', but 'ends' gives BUTTS and 'up' turns it to STTUB; that goes inside TEE (Tees 'unfinished'). The Tees is a river in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: A glass tube closed at one end is the classic laboratory container for experiments.

clue.text: Left plant in N. Ireland

parts.note: port is the left-hand side of a ship
a rush is a marsh plant

explanation.surface: Someone abandoned a plant somewhere in Northern Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' reads as 'abandoned', but it is PORT, the nautical left. The definition 'in N. Ireland' stands for a place there.
explanation.definitionFit: Portrush is a seaside resort town on the County Antrim coast of Northern Ireland.

clue.text: Oratorio was the making of Haydn

definitions.text: Oratorio was the making of Haydn

parts.words: Oratorio was the making of Haydn
parts.note: reads as a claim that one oratorio made Haydn's name, but 'the making' names his famous oratorio about Genesis

explanation.definitionFit: Haydn's oratorio 'Die Schöpfung' tells the Genesis story of God making the world.

clue.text: Somebody thinking about a rifle?

indicators.note: 'thinking about a' puts the thinker's letters around the A

parts.note: a muser is someone who muses, that is, thinks things over

explanation.surface: A person is wondering about a rifle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reads as 'concerning' but wraps MUSER around A.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mauser is a German bolt-action rifle, named after its makers.

clue.text: Get medical advice before writing in about nothing

parts.note: pre means before, as in prewar
script is handwriting or written text

indicators.note: 'in about nothing' puts the letters of in around the letter for nothing

parts.note: taken as written
O, the zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: Get a doctor's advice before you write anything about nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' sets IN around O to make ION, after PRE and SCRIPT.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor's written instruction for medicine is formal medical advice.

clue.text: Quarters for, retired artist

indicators.note: something retired has gone back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: pro means for, as in pros and cons
E and N are compass points, the quarters of the compass

explanation.surface: Living quarters set aside for a retired painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quarters' wants to be lodgings; it is two compass points, E and N. PRO reversed by 'retired' gives ORP. William Orpen was an Irish portrait painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir William Orpen was a portrait painter and official war artist in the First World War.

clue.text: Guide identified in a twinkling ?

parts.note: reads as a guide spotted instantly, but 'twinkling' is literal: a guide that twinkles in the sky

explanation.definitionFit: Polaris, the pole star, has long guided navigators because it marks true north.

clue.text: Loses opportunity of joining girls-but he's crazy !

parts.note: misses are girls or young women

indicators.note: crazy means wildly out of order, so the letters of but he's are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man misses his chance to join the girls, but he's mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crazy' rearranges BUT HE'S into THEBUS, after MISSES.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for failing to grab a chance, as one fails to catch a departing coach.

clue.text: An ore — the Scotch have a final check about it

parts.note: hae is the Scots form of have

indicators.note: 'about it' sets the word for the final check around the letters of it

parts.note: mate, as in checkmate, is the last check that ends a chess game
taken as written

explanation.surface: Scottish miners take one last look round the iron ore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'check' looks like an inspection; in chess the final check is MATE, wrapped around IT to make MAITTE, after HAE.
explanation.definitionFit: Haematite is the main ore of iron, a reddish iron oxide.

clue.text: Cunning person gives boys lots of diversion

indicators.note: a diversion is a turning aside, so the letters of boys and lots are turned into a new order

explanation.surface: A sly character gives the boys plenty of fun and games.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diversion' reads as amusement, but signals the rearrangement of BOYS LOTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Slyboots is a playful word for a crafty or mischievous person.

clue.text: I admit no interruption that's so ill-informed

indicators.note: an interruption breaks into something, so no goes into the middle of the word for admit

parts.note: to grant is to admit or concede a point
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone admits there was no interruption, which shows how little they know.
explanation.walkthrough: NO interrupts GRANT to give GNORANT, after I.
explanation.definitionFit: To be ignorant is to lack knowledge, to be uninformed.

clue.text: Roe brings Lea fresh fruit

indicators.note: fresh means new, so the letters are made into something new

explanation.surface: Someone called Roe brings Lea some fresh fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fresh' looks like it describes the fruit, but it rearranges the letters of ROE BRINGS LEA.
explanation.definitionFit: These are hybrid berries, a cross between the raspberry and the blackberry.

clue.text: She is after the admiral's heart early in the morning

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central part, here of the word admiral
early means at the start, taking the opening letter of the word in

parts.note: AM, ante meridiem, means the morning

explanation.surface: A woman is chasing the admiral's affections at dawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'early in' reads as 'at the start of the morning', but 'early' picks I from 'in'; MIR is the centre of ADMIRAL, and 'the morning' is AM.
explanation.definitionFit: Miriam is a female name, borne by the sister of Moses, so it stands for a woman.

clue.text: Brief state meeting concerning flag

parts.note: Penn is a short form of Pennsylvania, a US state
on means about or concerning, as in a talk on art

explanation.surface: A short state meeting held to discuss a flag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'meeting' joins the two pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A pennon is a long narrow pointed banner, once carried on a lance.

clue.text: Halted and reared ?

explanation.definitionFit: To be pulled up short is to be stopped; children raised by parents are nurtured into adults.

clue.text: Land with 1 ac in jungle belt ?

indicators.note: 'in jungle belt' says the letters sit inside those two words

explanation.surface: A patch of land beside a parsonage lies in a jungle zone.
explanation.walkthrough: 1 ac refers to the answer at 1 across, the priest's house: this is the land that goes with it.
explanation.definitionFit: Glebe is the land belonging to a parish church, providing income for the incumbent.

clue.text: A show of swank put across by an actor

parts.note: side is an old word for swagger or pretension, as in 'putting on side'

explanation.surface: An actor puts on a show of swagger for the audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Side' meaning swank is British and dated: someone with no side has no airs.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor's remark to the audience, unheard by the other characters, is delivered across the stage.

clue.text: Lear character gets nothing back,-the ass !

parts.note: O, the zero, means nothing

indicators.note: back means the daughter's name is read in the backwards direction

parts.note: Regan is one of King Lear's daughters in Shakespeare's play

explanation.surface: A character in King Lear gets nothing in return and is called an ass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns REGAN into NAGER, after O.
explanation.definitionFit: An onager is a wild ass of central Asia.

clue.text: A bit of army arithmetic ?

parts.note: two readings meet: a unit that is part of an army, and one of the four sums done in arithmetic

explanation.definitionFit: An army formation of several brigades shares its name with the sum that splits a number into equal parts.

clue.text: Camp follower said to be craftier

indicators.note: said to be means the word for craftier is spoken and heard, not written

parts.note: subtler means more crafty or cunning

explanation.surface: A hanger-on in a military camp is reported to be more cunning.
explanation.walkthrough: SUBTLER said with its B silent sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A sutler was a trader who followed an army and sold provisions to soldiers.

clue.text: Writer's material distorted :Marne battle

parts.note: ink is what a writer uses

indicators.note: distorted means twisted out of shape, so the letters of Marne are rearranged

explanation.surface: A pen's ink is smudged in a report of the Battle of the Marne.
explanation.walkthrough: The Marne is a decoy battle; 'distorted' rearranges it to ERMAN after INK. Inkerman was a battle of the Crimean War, 1854.
explanation.definitionFit: Inkerman was an 1854 Crimean War clash where British and French troops beat the Russians.
